                         1.0 Introduction and Scope
                         In accordance with the requirements of Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) Part
                         50, SMR, LLC is submitting this Enclosure IV as a compilation of the specific exemption requests
                         on behalf of Palisades SMR, LLC (Palisades SMR or applicant). Enclosure IV is in support of the
                         Construction Permit Application (CPA), Part II, for Pioneer Units 1 and 2, the dual-unit SMR-300
                         plant to be constructed at the Palisades Energy Center (PEC) in Covert, Michigan.
                         Each exemption request is prepared in accordance with 10 CFR 50.12 [Ref. 1]. Each request
                         follows a common structure consisting of the Proposed Exemption, Background, Detailed
                         Description, Justification for Exemption addressing the three findings of 10 CFR 50.12(a)(1)
                         together with Proposed Rulemaking and Past Precedent, Special Circumstances under 10 CFR
                         50.12(a)(2), and Conclusion.
                         This Enclosure IV requests that the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) grant the
                         following exemptions in support of the CPA and coincident with issuance of the construction
                         permit associated with this application.

                         1.1 Regulatory Basis for the Requested Exemptions
                         10 CFR 50.12(a) provides that the Commission may, upon application by any interested person or
                         upon its own initiative, grant exemptions from the requirements of the regulations of 10 CFR Part
                         50 which are:
                                   •         Authorized by law,
                                   •         Will not present an undue risk to the public health and safety, and
                             • Are consistent with the common defense and security.
                         These are the three findings of 10 CFR 50.12(a)(1) that must be made to grant an exemption. 10
                         CFR 50.12(a)(2) further provides that the Commission will not consider granting an exemption
                         unless special circumstances are present. Each request in this enclosure addresses all three findings
                         of 10 CFR 50.12(a)(1) and identifies the applicable special circumstances of 10 CFR 50.12(a)(2).
                         Each exemption is requested for Pioneer Units 1 and 2 only. None of the requested exemptions is
                         generic in nature, and none is requested for any other facility. Granting the requested exemptions
                         would not authorize any activity beyond those otherwise authorized by the construction permit,
                         and each exemption would remain subject to the conditions of the permit and to NRC inspection
                         and oversight.
                         This Enclosure IV has evaluated the requested exemptions collectively as well as individually. The
                         exemptions address independent regulatory subject areas, with the exception of the emergency
                         preparedness exemptions in Sections 2.0 and 3.0, which are related as described in those sections.
                         No combination of the requested exemptions results in a cumulative effect on public health and
                         safety or on the common defense and security beyond the effect of each request considered
                         individually.

                         2.0 Exemption Request, 10 CFR 50.34(a)(10)(i), 10 CFR 50.47, and App. E
                         2.1 Proposed Exemption
                         In accordance with the requirements of 10 CFR 50.12, SMR, LLC, on behalf of Palisades SMR,
                         LLC, hereby requests exemption from 10 CFR 50.34(a)(10)(i) and from the otherwise applicable
                         requirements of 10 CFR 50.47 and Appendix E to 10 CFR Part 50 [Ref. 3], for Pioneer Units 1
                         and 2, the dual-unit SMR-300 plant to be constructed at the PEC in Covert, Michigan.
                         The requested exemption would permit SMR, LLC to develop and describe the preliminary plans
                         for coping with emergencies, and subsequently the emergency plan, in accordance with the
                         performance-based emergency preparedness (EP) requirements of 10 CFR 50.160 in lieu of the
                         requirements of 10 CFR 50.47 and Appendix E to 10 CFR Part 50.
                         SMR, LLC requests that the NRC grant this exemption in support of the CPA and coincident with
                         issuance of the construction permit associated with this application.

                         2.2 Background
                         The NRC regulatory frameworks for EP for nuclear power reactors are established in 10 CFR Part
                         50. A long-standing deterministic framework, applicable to the existing fleet of large light-water
                         reactors (LWRs), is provided in 10 CFR 50.47 and Appendix E to 10 CFR Part 50. An alternative
                         performance-based EP framework became available in 2023 when the NRC promulgated 10 CFR
                         50.160. Relief from 10 CFR 50.47 and Appendix E to 10 CFR Part 50 is also necessary because
                         those provisions would otherwise continue to establish the governing emergency preparedness
                         requirements for the SMR-300.
                         10 CFR 50.34(a)(10) establishes the EP content requirement for a preliminary safety analysis
                         report (PSAR) and states that the PSAR must include a discussion of the applicant’s preliminary
                         plans for coping with emergencies based on:
                                             “(i) Except as provided in paragraph (a)(10)(ii) of this section, the requirements in
                                             appendix E to this part, or (ii) For a small modular reactor, a non-light-water reactor, or
                                             non-power production or utilization facility construction permit applicant, the
                                             requirements in either § 50.160 or appendix E to this part.”
                         10 CFR 50.34(a)(10)(i) is therefore the requirement that binds the applicant at the construction
                         permit stage. The option provided by 10 CFR 50.34(a)(10)(ii) is available only to applicants
                         meeting the 10 CFR 50.2 definition of “small modular reactor,” which limits thermal power
                         capacity to “up to 1,000 megawatts thermal power per module.” Because each SMR-300 unit
                         produces up to 1,050 megawatts thermal (MWth), the SMR-300 does not qualify for that option
                         as the regulation is currently written. Exemption from 10 CFR 50.34(a)(10)(i) is accordingly
                         necessary to permit the preliminary emergency plans to be based on 10 CFR 50.160. The need for
                         this exemption arises solely from the thermal-power criterion in the 10 CFR 50.2 definition of
                         ‘small modular reactor’ and not from any limitation associated with the SMR-300 emergency
                         preparedness design or the performance-based requirements of 10 CFR 50.160.
                         SMR, LLC is not requesting an exemption from the definition in 10 CFR 50.2. A definition is not
                         itself an actionable requirement. The requested relief is directed at the substantive provisions that

                         2.3 Detailed Description
                         The proposed exemption would allow SMR, LLC to use the EP framework of 10 CFR 50.160 for
                         the SMR-300 plant in lieu of 10 CFR 50.47 and Appendix E to 10 CFR Part 50. The SMR-300
                         emergency plan will be developed to meet the performance-based requirements of 10 CFR
                         50.160(b) in their entirety, including the performance-based framework, the emergency response
                         performance functions, the EPZ determination, the drill and exercise provisions, and the
                         emergency action level scheme. The preliminary plans for coping with emergencies developed on
                         this basis are described in PSAR Section 13.3.
                         Apart from the per-unit thermal power margin described above, the SMR-300 has the design
                         attributes the Commission associated with the class of reactors for which 10 CFR 50.160 was
                         promulgated. These attributes include a modular, factory-fabricated design, passive safety systems
                         that do not rely on pumps, external water supplies, offsite power, or credited operator action to
                         reach and maintain safe shutdown, and correspondingly lower core damage frequency, large
                         release frequency, and radiological source term than the operating large-LWR fleet. Accordingly,
                         the SMR-300 possesses the same design attributes that formed the basis for the Commission’s

                         Approved Methodology Supporting the Emergency Preparedness Basis
                         The radiological consequence basis underlying the SMR-300 EP approach rests on an NRC-
                         approved, design-specific methodology. The NRC has approved Licensing Topical Report (LTR)
                         HI-2241098-A [Ref. 5].
                         The approved LTR provides a site-independent methodology for determining the accident
                         consequences from design basis accidents (DBAs) required to be evaluated under 10 CFR 50.34.
                         The methodology is used to determine the total effective dose equivalent at the exclusion area
                         boundary, the low population zone, the main control room, and the technical support center. The
                         methodology generally follows Regulatory Guide (RG) 1.183 [Ref. 6], and the NRC found that,
                         where the methodology applies case-by-case approaches, SMR, LLC provided adequate technical
                         justifications. The approved methodology also confirms the acceptability of the treatment of the
                         in-containment spent fuel pool (SFP) for DBA consequence analysis and the acceptability of the
                         iodine chemical form assumptions for the SMR-300 containment flood-up pool.
                         The offsite dose consequences supporting the SMR-300 EP program will therefore be developed
                         using a method the NRC has already accepted. This supports both the use of the 10 CFR 50.160
                         framework requested in this section and the deferral of the site-specific EPZ sizing analysis
                         addressed in Section 3.0.

                         2.4 Justification for Exemption
                         In accordance with 10 CFR 50.12, the Commission may, upon application by any interested person
                         or upon its own initiative, grant exemptions from the requirements of the regulations of 10 CFR
                         Part 50 that are authorized by law, will not present an undue risk to the public health and safety,
                         and are consistent with the common defense and security. 10 CFR 50.12 also states that the
                         Commission will not consider granting an exemption unless special circumstances are present. As
                         discussed below, the requested exemption satisfies these criteria.
                         2.4.1 Criteria of 10 CFR 50.12(a)(1)
                         The Exemption is Authorized by Law
                         The requested exemption from 10 CFR 50.34(a)(10)(i), 10 CFR 50.47, and Appendix E to 10 CFR
                         Part 50 does not result in a violation of the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended, or the
                         Commission’s regulations. 10 CFR 50.12 allows the NRC to grant exemptions from the
                         requirements of 10 CFR Part 50. Therefore, this exemption is authorized by law.
                         The Exemption Will Not Present an Undue Risk to the Public Health and Safety

                         systems, does not alter accident initiators, does not create new accident precursors, does not impact
                         the consequences of any design-basis event, and does not affect the performance or reliability of
                         power operations. The exemption determines only which of two NRC-established EP frameworks

                         also does not require heat-affected-zone specimens, which have been shown to be of limited value.

                         use of the master curve method described in ASTM E1921 [Ref. 46], which can reduce
                         measurement uncertainty and support evaluation of extended plant operational lifetimes.
                         Over the past 60 years, reactor vessel embrittlement mechanisms and their underlying causes have
                         been extensively studied, and the value of measuring reactor vessel transition temperature shifts at
                         low fluences has diminished as operating experience has evolved. Controlling certain deleterious
                         elements, namely copper and nickel, in the vessel forgings and in weld filler metals has alleviated
                         many problems associated with reactor vessel embrittlement experienced in some earlier nuclear
                         power plants. Therefore, withdrawing surveillance capsules at evenly spaced intervals based on
                         the design life of the reactor is a practical method for measuring and managing reactor vessel
                         aging, as compared with the approach prescribed in ASTM E185-82, which is biased toward
                         measuring low-fluence transition temperature shifts in a reactor vessel with an assumed
                         operational lifetime of 40 years.
                         Compatibility of the ASTM E185-21 Withdrawal Schedule with Appendix H
                         Use of the ASTM E185-21 withdrawal schedule could raise the question of whether it conflicts
                         with the expectation that the first three surveillance capsules be withdrawn within the first 40 years
                         of operation. Under ASTM E185-21, the withdrawal schedule is expressed in terms of fractions of
                         the maximum design fluence (MDF) rather than in elapsed operating time, with capsules
                         withdrawn at one-quarter, one-half, three-quarters, and the full MDF, plus a standby capsule.
                         The accumulated fluence at a given capsule location is governed by the capsule radial position and
                         the associated lead factor, so the timing of each withdrawal is a design variable. ASTM E185-21
                         permits lead factors in the range of 1.5 to 5, compared with 1 to 3 under ASTM E185-82. The
                         SMR-300 surveillance capsules are positioned to achieve lead factors within the ASTM E185-21
                         range such that the first three capsules reach their respective fluence-based withdrawal points, and
                         are withdrawn and tested within the first 40 years of operation. No conflict therefore arises between
                         the fluence-based withdrawal schedule of ASTM E185-21 and the withdrawal timing expectations
                         underlying Appendix H, and surveillance data remain available to support the Appendix G fracture
                         toughness evaluations throughout the 80-year operational lifetime. Accordingly, the underlying
                         purpose of Appendix H continues to be achieved through the proposed surveillance program.
